summary: Two independent R3 design reviews agree that v22/v19 preserve the repaired post-Bootstrap slot, held-lock, and official-result foundations, but six remaining normal-failure paths are still implementation-blocking: pre-E quality policy provenance/topology, fork-safe held-lock lifetime, control-chain materialization and partial recovery, ChildReceipt author-versus-publisher handoff, post-S5 acceptance recovery, and the sealed adapter for the unchanged path-only mechanics worker.

limitations: The consolidated result only records independent read-only findings and does not change the reviewed design.

No product/test/contract/gate/ledger/status/historical-evidence implementation changed; no project-code execution, training, archival replay, budget consumption, PIT certification, M7 or final-OOS access occurred.

blockers: Make the pre-E release policy an observed immutable root with a fixed quality-slot topology, anchor/root/parent D-v2 identity chains, policy bytes/ref equality, and an exact M6.5 gate-evidence role map before Bootstrap/PASS publication.
Make the held control lock process-bound across fork with owner PID/generation checks, child at-fork poison/close, and an explicit close-all plus FD allow-list launch protocol.
Specify a locked replay-supervisor materialization/recovery API for E/C and C-to-P/F-to-A-to-B-to-Q partial chains, with deterministic byte-equality and no generic publisher.

Replace the contradictory ChildReceipt writer rule with a frozen child-attestation / supervisor-durable-envelope handoff, including kernel-authenticated IPC, raw-receipt binding, lock ownership, and crash behavior.
Define deterministic lock-held recovery for ArchiveAcceptanceReceipt, S6, and FinalIndex partial-publication windows.
Define a SlotSpec-bound scratch/staging adapter that supplies the unchanged mechanics worker only an adapter-derived path, never arbitrary caller paths or the official output root.
Reissue architecture and change design, then obtain fresh independent R3 design-review PASS before test design, red tests, implementation, code review, replay, M7, CCC/Gate, or final-OOS work.
